topic.title: Contributing Code Templates from a Framework

body.p: Aside from the code templates that you define in the Preferences dialog box, a framework can also contribute its own code templates. They are stored as individual XML files inside the framework directory, so they travel with the framework and are available to everyone who uses it, without requiring each user to import them. This is useful for document type-specific fragments, such as a table skeleton or the steps of a task.
body.note: To have the code templates proposed in all editors, regardless of the framework, use the Additional code templates folder option from the Editor Content Completion Code Templates preferences page instead. The files have the same structure.
body.p: The code templates contributed by a framework are proposed in the Content Completion Assistant, in both Text and Author mode, but only for documents that are associated with that framework. They are marked with the same symbol as the other code templates. They are not listed in the Editor Content Completion Code Templates preferences page because they are not stored in the application options and are not meant to be edited there.

section.title: Where to Store the Code Template Files

ul.li: {framework_directory}/resources/codeTemplates - If multiple *.framework files are located in {framework_directory}, this folder structure makes the code templates available to all of them.

{framework_directory}/resources/codeTemplates/{framework_file_name} - This folder structure makes the code templates available only to the framework stored in the {framework_file_name}.framework file. The subfolders of this folder are also scanned, so you can organize the templates in any way you choose.

section.p: The framework also searches for a codeTemplates folder in each folder listed on its Classpath tab. Most frameworks already include a ${framework}/resources/ classpath entry, which resolves to the same folder described above. This is also how a framework that extends another one inherits the shared code templates of its base framework, because it inherits the base framework's classpath entries.
section.note: A framework extension inherits only the code templates stored directly in the codeTemplates folder of its base framework. The framework-specific subfolder is always searched using the extension's file name, including within the base framework's folders. For example, a myDita.exf extension of the DITA framework searches for codeTemplates/myDita, so templates stored in codeTemplates/dita are not proposed. To make those templates available in the extension, copy them to the extension's resources/codeTemplates folder.

If the same code template is contributed from multiple locations, the template from the most specific location is used. A template stored in the framework-specific folder replaces a template with the same name and content type from the shared folder or a base framework.

section.title: The Structure of a Code Template File
section.p: Each file defines a single code template, using the codeTemplate element from the http://www.oxygenxml.com/ns/code-template namespace. The easiest way to create such a file is to open the new document wizard (New toolbar button), search for a template called Code Template, and save the resulting file in one of the folders presented above.

fig.title: Example of a Code Template File
fig.codeblock: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ct:codeTemplate xmlns:ct="http://www.oxygenxml.com/ns/code-template"> <ct:name>dita-note</ct:name> <ct:description>Inserts a note.</ct:description> <ct:contentType>text/xml</ct:contentType> <ct:accelerator>M1 M2 M3 N</ct:accelerator> <ct:content xml:space="preserve"><![CDATA[<note type="note">${caret}</note>]]></ct:content> </ct:codeTemplate>

section.p:
The following elements can be used:
name - The name of the code template. This is the text that you type in the editor to have the template proposed. To avoid confusion with the element names proposed by the associated schema, it is recommended that you use a distinctive prefix, such as dita-table rather than table.
description - [Optional] The description of the code template, shown in the documentation window of the Content Completion Assistant.
contentType - [Optional] The type of editor in which the code template is proposed, for example text/xml, text/css, or text/json. When it is missing, the template is proposed in all editors associated with the contributing framework.
accelerator - [Optional] A shortcut key that inserts the code template directly. It is specified in a platform-independent form, and the following modifiers are used:
Make sure the shortcut is not already used by another action, otherwise it will not be triggered.
content - The content that is inserted in the editor. White space is preserved exactly as it appears in the file, so keep the xml:space="preserve" attribute. Since the content is inserted as plain text, any markup must be escaped or placed inside a CDATA section. An editor variable can be used, with ${caret} marking the position where the cursor is left after insertion.

section.title: How to Test the Code Templates
section.p: Open a document that is associated with your framework and invoke the Content Completion Assistant (Enter in Author mode or in Text mode). In Text mode, you can also press to see only the code templates. To refine a template, open its XML file in , make changes, save the file, and then test it again.You can also add or edit the code template files outside of , but you will need to restart the application to reload the changes.
